ai.subject: Pathology
ai.summary: Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease is a hereditary disorder causing bilateral renal cysts that enlarge kidneys, impair function, and predispose to hypertension, pain, and aneurysms. It follows a classic diagnostic triad of family history, imaging, and cyst count. Management focuses on blood pressure control, pain relief, and monitoring for complications.

sections.p: ADPKD is a genetic disorder with cystic dilatation of renal tubules, leading to enlarged kidneys and progressive renal failure. Diagnosis relies on imaging and family history.
b: Cysts >4 on each kidney or >2 on one kidney in a first‑degree relative

t.b: Detects cysts and kidney size; normal in early disease
Quantifies cyst number and size; useful when ultrasound equivocal
Confirms PKD1 or PKD2 mutation; guides counseling when imaging is inconclusive

sections.p: Kidney function is staged by eGFR and cyst burden. Early stages show normal eGFR; later stages have reduced filtration and increased cyst volume.
b: Kidney Failure Risk Equation (KFRE) predicts progression

t.b: Assesses renal function; decline indicates progression
Higher volume correlates with faster decline

sections.p: ADPKD is autosomal dominant, caused by mutations in PKD1 (85%) or PKD2 (15%).
b: PKD1: large gene, more severe disease

t.b: First‑degree relative with cystic kidneys or ESRD
Can worsen renal function but not cause cysts

sections.p: Patients often have flank pain, hematuria, hypertension, or are asymptomatic until adulthood.
b: Pain from cyst expansion or infection

t.b: Microscopic hematuria suggests cyst rupture or infection

sections.p: Work‑up focuses on imaging, renal function, and screening for extra‑renal complications.

sections.p: Urgent signs include sudden severe headache (possible aneurysm), gross hematuria, or rapidly rising creatinine.

sections.p: Treat hypertension, pain, and complications while monitoring renal function. Avoid nephrotoxic drugs and manage blood pressure aggressively.

Use acetaminophen; avoid NSAIDs to protect kidneys

sections.p: Regular monitoring of kidney size, function, and blood pressure. Counsel on lifestyle and avoid nephrotoxins.

t.b: Track decline; early intervention if >30% drop

sections.p: Differential includes autosomal recessive PKD, medullary cystic disease, and acquired cystic kidney disease.
b: Autosomal recessive PKD: early onset, severe disease
Acquired cystic disease: seen in dialysis patients

sections.p: Normal creatinine can mask early dysfunction; cysts may be missed on ultrasound if small.
